A_retention_while_draining.claim: A method of controlling therapeutic exposure in the CSF of a patient via an endovascular CSF-to-venous shunt, comprising: delivering a therapeutic agent into the CSF via the shunt; selectively retaining said agent via a size-selective element that permits CSF passage while retaining molecules above a threshold; maintaining clinically adequate CSF drainage through said shunt; wherein therapeutic exposure is increased relative to unretained delivery while drainage is preserved.
A_retention_while_draining.design_around_risk: MEDIUM — retention mechanisms exist in other contexts but not in eShunt
A_retention_while_draining.eShunt_specific: PARTIALLY — works in any shunt, but venous boundary (L6) adds eShunt specificity

B_retention_plus_separation.claim: The method of claim A, further comprising: delivering said agent at a location separated from the dominant CSF drainage path, wherein the combination of separation and retention creates controlled therapeutic residence.
B_retention_plus_separation.novelty: L3 (separation) is NOT novel (found in 2 CereVasc patents). L4 is novel. Combination untested.

C_retention_plus_adaptive.claim: The method of claim A, further comprising: estimating CSF drug concentration from hydraulic state and dosing history; adjusting drug delivery based on said estimate; maintaining CSF drainage throughout.
C_retention_plus_adaptive.novelty: UNKNOWN — needs separate hostile analysis. Not assumed patentable.
C_retention_plus_adaptive.note: C connects Position #1 (hydraulic state estimation) with Position #3 (drug delivery). Potential platform invention. Needs its own search later.
